```{r setup, eval = FALSE}
library(plant)
source("harness/long_drought.R")   # rainfall records and mkenv()
p <- scm_base_parameters("TF24")
p <- add_strategies(p, trait_matrix(0.32, "lma"))
```

# The whole thing

The quantities a run reports are J, a strategy's fitness (its offspring per seed over a
patch's life), and J's gradient with respect to each trait. Each has a tolerance ε, set
once per quantity (`docs/measurements/eps-spread.md`).

Every one of them is a sum over birth date, so a node schedule is a rule for that sum.
The schedule has two parts:

- **Breakpoints:** births where a recruit's fate is not smooth in birth date. These are
  the ends of each establishment spell, and on some records the birth date after which
  cohorts stall under the canopy. Each run's own establishment record gives the spell
  ends.
- **A count of intervals per spell.** Each spell's nodes are placed at equal shares of a
  density that says where fate curves most.

A run estimates its own error. Replay it on its own steps with every other node inside
each spell removed. A third of the change estimates the run's error, in every quantity at
once. If any quantity is over its limit, raise the counts and run again. The last run is
the answer.

```{r whole, eval = FALSE}
fit <- refine_schedule(p, mkenv("episodic"))
fit$answer     # J and its gradient, from the last run
fit$estimate   # each quantity's estimated error, from that run's replay
fit$schedule   # breakpoints, counts per spell, node times
fit$history    # each pass: its schedule, answer, estimate; and why the loop stopped
```

# What a node is

On the birth-date coordinate a node is the cohort born at one instant. The individuals
born between two neighbouring nodes form an interval, and the interval carries two
things:

- **Its count.** The run integrates the establishment rate exactly over the interval,
  together with its first moment.
- **Its members' fate.** Their survival, size and seed output are taken to vary linearly
  in birth date between the two nodes.

Every stand total has the same form: J, the leaf area above a height, the water drawn
from a soil layer. Each is a sum over intervals of count × interpolated fate.

The schedule's error is the error of that sum:

- **Where fate is smooth across an interval,** the error is about
  count × width² × fate's curvature, so it falls four-fold when the spacing halves.
- **The error adds over birth date.** Errors measured region by region add to the whole
  run's within 0.04ε.
- **A local error reaches every cohort.** An interval that over-counts leaf area or
  uptake changes the light and water every other cohort meets.

# Breakpoints

**Net production decides everything.** An individual's net production is

    P = a_bio · a_y · (A − R) − T

where A is the leaf's optimal assimilation, set by the light at its crown and the water
its roots reach. P drives each process:

- **P > 0:** the individual grows and fills its storage pool.
- **P < 0:** the pool drains, and the hazard a_dG1 · exp(−a_dG2 · r) rises as relative
  storage r falls.
- **Establishment:** a newborn establishes only if its P at seed height is positive.

A seedling's roots lie in the top 0.3 m of soil, so establishment follows the top
layer's water. A rain starts an establishment spell within a day, and the stand's uptake
dries the layer until the spell ends. Between spells nothing establishes.

**At a spell's opening, fate's slope jumps.**
- A cohort born just before an opening waits for rain, so a later birth waits less and
  does better.
- After the opening, each later cohort meets more shade, so it does worse.
- On dry, fate's slope was +0.5e-3 per day before every one of 22 openings and
  −2.2e-3 per day after.

**At a spell's end, the count stops.**
- Fate itself is continuous there. Within the spell its curvature rises 1.3–5× toward
  the end, and the cohorts' sensitivity to the hydraulic traits curves up to 17× harder.
- An interval that reaches past the end into the gap takes its members' fate from the gap's different curve.
  Its error is then set by how far its last node sits from the end, not by the spacing.

So both ends of every spell are breakpoints. With them, the worst errors on dry,
long-wet and episodic with lma ×1.25 fell from 1.1–3.4ε to 0.47–0.79ε.

**A spell's end moves with the schedule.** The end is where the stand's uptake dries the
top layer, and that uptake depends on the nodes. Ends moved by a median of 0.48 days
between passes, and the first spell's end by 12 days; openings did not move. So each run
takes its spell ends from its own establishment record, and the next pass's breakpoints
come from the last run, not from the first.

**On constant rain there is one more breakpoint.**
- Cohorts born in the first 23.5 days reach the canopy.
- Every later cohort stalls under them: its P falls below zero and comes back.
- Survival to the end of the run falls from 0.63 to 0.02 across 0.03 days of birth date.

In the model's equations, fate stops being smooth only where a cohort's sequence of P
sign changes differs from its neighbour's (`docs/dynamics.md`).
- With a diagnostic build that counts each node's sign changes, the count goes from 0 to
  2 exactly at the stall.
- Five rounds of forward runs with about 100 nodes, each bisecting the pair whose counts
  differ, place the stall to 0.0003 day.
- Today's runs do not record that count.

**Finding spell ends.** A forward run on about 100 even introductions places 98–100% of
openings within a day of the finest run's, and 75–89% of ends. The ends then move to
their own run's values each pass.

# The count per spell and the density

A breakpoint is never removed. Between breakpoints, each spell gets an even number of
intervals, and its nodes sit at equal shares of a density. Four shapes in fate set the
density:

- **The first cohorts.** Births before the first spell ends produce 70–97% of J. Their
  fate falls nearly exponentially in birth date, with a decay length of 0.4–1.2 years,
  because a later birth reproduces later, against the patch's disturbance and the stand's
  drought mortality.
- **The understory.**
  - Within a spell, a later birth is a smaller copy that has had less time to die, so its
    leaf area is convex in birth date.
  - Straight lines between nodes over-count that leaf area by 0.5–1.1% (3–4% in the
    first years). Through the light or the water the stand creates (the measurements
    disagree on which), the first cohorts carry most of that error as extra drought
    mortality.
- **The last three weeks of a spell.** A seedling born there starts the coming drought
  with fuller reserves, and every one of them empties its reserves. The cohorts'
  sensitivity to the hydraulic and storage traits curves 3–17× harder than a month
  earlier. The density rises to about 2× over the last 18 days, back to 1 by 27 days
  before the end, and each spell gets two more intervals for it.
- **Late births.** They produce little J but still draw down the water. Late intervals
  wider than about 160 days leave the square law on the traits that act through the soil.

The first density is graded by the offspring curve, and its ages come from T(t), the
share of J still to be produced after calendar time t:
- the onset of seed output ends the first cohorts' fine spacing;
- the time half of J has been produced is where the spacing cap changes;
- the time 90% has been produced is where late spacing may widen.

On the ten-case bank these land at about 10, 16–24 and 23–29 years, where fixed ages had
put them. In a shorter run they move earlier with it.

**A spell too short to hold two intervals** keeps one, and the replay does not see it.
Such spells hold much of the establishment but 0.5–6.6% of J; on three cases their error
was 0.05–0.10ε. No bound for it works yet.

# How a run estimates its own error

Remove every other node inside each spell, and replay the run on its own steps:

    estimated error ≈ (Q with every other node removed − Q) / 3

Why it can be trusted:

- **Every interval is merged once.** Each spell holds an even number of intervals, so
  the removal merges them all in pairs. With an odd count, one interval per spell is
  never merged; in the first tests that hid 17 of 70 spell ends, and 39 more sat in
  spells with no node inside to remove.
- **Each removed node sits at the middle of what it merges, by share of the density.**
  The factor 1/3 is exact for a node at the middle in width. Off the middle it is
  (l³ + (1 − l)³)/(3 l (1 − l)) for a node at fraction l. With the graded density the
  replay estimated the error at 0.97 of its size in one run on dry.
- **The replay shares the run's steps,** so step-size choices add nothing to the
  difference.
- **The replay includes the stand's response.** A removed node changes the light and
  water every cohort meets, and the replay recomputes that.
- **Measured:** with both spell ends as breakpoints, the estimate was 0.75–0.87 of the
  error (cosine 0.88–0.97) on dry, long-wet and episodic with lma ×1.25, and never
  passed a run that was over ε. With the grading before spell ends it was 0.97 on dry.
- **Cost:** 0.55–0.64 of a run.

What the replay cannot see:
- **The run's own ODE tolerance error,** because the replay shares the run's steps. At
  1e-4 that error was at most 0.11ε on five cases (3e-5 cuts it but costs 1.4× the steps).
- **Spells too short to hold two intervals.**
- **Errors in its own estimate:** it estimated the error at 0.75–0.97 of its size.

So the loop holds every quantity to 0.88ε, not ε, at 1e-4.

**Where the error is.** The run's own reverse sweep, with a small addition, also gives
J's error by stretch of birth date, to 0.03ε, for 7.5% more than the run.

# The loop

```
  first run (about 100 even introductions, forward only)
        │ establishment spells, offspring curve, T(t)
        ▼
  breakpoints (spell ends; the stall boundary, if any, by bisection passes)
  + first density and an even count per spell
        │
        ▼
  run ──► replay with every other node in each spell removed ──► estimated error
   │  │                                                          of each quantity
   │  └► reverse sweep ──► where J's error is
   ▼
  every quantity's estimated error under 0.88ε?
        │ yes: this run is the answer
        │ no:  take spell ends from this run, scale every spell's count by
        │      1.1 × √(worst estimate / 0.88ε), keep counts even, make sure the
        │      spells holding the worst error change, and run again
```

- **Every full run is a candidate answer;** no run is made only to be compared with.
- **Doubling every count makes each run the previous one's removal case.** The previous
  run then estimates the new one without a replay. On dry it estimated the error at 1.04
  of its size, with step noise of 0.004–0.012 rms at 3e-5.
- **It stops.** On the square law each scaling cuts the worst ratio by the square of the
  scale. The margin of 1.1 and the forced change keep it from stalling at the boundary,
  and a cap on passes reports a failure instead of running on.

# What it adapts to

| what varies | why | what responds |
|---|---|---|
| when spells start and end | the rainfall record and the stand's uptake | breakpoints, taken from each run's own establishment record |
| where cohorts stall | the canopy on constant rain | a breakpoint, placed by bisection passes |
| where fate curves | first cohorts, understory, a spell's last weeks, late births | the density and the count per spell |
| how large the error is | about 100× across trait × climate | the replay estimates it on each run |
| which quantities bind | different traits on different cases | every quantity has its own ε |
| how a local error spreads | light and water reach every cohort | the replay recomputes the stand's response |
| simulation length | when J is produced | the first density's ages, from T(t) |

# Traits

The traits move the breakpoints by moving where P = 0:
- Carbon gain, carbon cost and water access set the light and water at which P
  vanishes, and so when spells start and end.
- Height growth sets who ends up shaded.
- The storage pool sets how costly a time below zero is.

On constant rain:
- lma ×0.8 and ×1.25 move the stall from day 23.6 to 27.1 and 18.9;
- hmat ×0.8 and ×1.25 move it to days 45–50 and 9.9–10.9.

A schedule refined at one set of traits serves nearby ones, but the error grows as the
traits move. Checking a moved trait on the shared schedule costs a run at those traits
plus its replay.

# Still being tested

- the width of the grading before spell ends, taken from the first run instead of from
  fate maps on dry, and the full layout on more cases;
- dry-flat's understory, where region replays estimated 1.9× the error;
- a bound for spells too short to hold two intervals;
- which of light or water carries the understory's error.

Settled so far:
- fate's slope jumps only at openings, but spell ends need breakpoints as well;
- with even counts every interval is merged, and the replay costs 0.55–0.64 of a run;
- the last weeks of a spell need a graded density with more intervals, not a breakpoint
  of their own: on dry that took the worst error from 0.79 to 0.36ε (E6, today's tuned
  schedule: 0.35) and the estimate to 0.97 of the error.
